questions.question: Dr. Sami receives a patient with irreversible pulpitis. He tells Mina: 'I'm going to do a root canal, it's simple.' Mina asks him: 'Are you sure about that?' What is the definition of root canal treatment?
options: Removal of the pulp and obturation of the canal space
Placement of a crown on a devitalized tooth
Extraction of the tooth to prevent infection
questions.explanation: Sami explains: 'Root canal treatment consists of removing the infected pulp, cleaning and disinfecting the canals, then filling them.' Mina adds: 'Hopefully you don't miss any canals.'

questions.question: Mina examines a patient and finds a deep cavity with pulp exposure. She decides to perform a pulpectomy. Sami, curious, asks her: 'What exactly is a pulpectomy?' Mina answers:
options: Removal of coronal and radicular pulp
Disinfection of the canal without removal
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Pulpectomy is the complete removal of the pulp, including in the root canals.' Sami retorts: 'I knew that, I just wanted to test you.'

questions.question: Sami, in his haste, forgets to place a rubber dam on a patient. Mina stops him: 'Sami, the rubber dam is mandatory!' Sami asks: 'Why?' Mina explains:
options: To isolate the tooth, prevent contamination, and protect the airway
To make the consultation last longer
questions.explanation: Mina is firm: 'The rubber dam isolates the tooth, prevents salivary contamination, and protects the patient from inhaling small instruments.' Sami, slightly annoyed, places it.

questions.question: Mina begins canal instrumentation. Sami, observing her, asks: 'Why are you using a manual file and not the machine?' Mina answers:
options: To feel the canal morphology and avoid errors
Because I don't trust the machine
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The manual file allows you to feel the curvatures, calcifications, and canal length. It's safer to avoid ledges.' Sami, impressed, takes notes.

questions.question: Sami uses a rotary file. Mina asks him: 'Are you sure you calibrated your file correctly?' Sami answers: 'Of course!' Mina retorts: 'Why is that important?'
options: To avoid file fracture or excessive enlargement
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Inadequate calibration can fracture the file in the canal or create excessive apical enlargement.' Sami, slightly worried, checks his calibration.

questions.question: Sami, confidently, announces to Mina that he has finished his root canal treatment. Mina asks him: 'And the working length, how did you check it?' Sami answers:
options: With an apex locator and a radiograph
With the naked eye, as always
With a ruler on the radiograph
questions.explanation: Mina confirms: 'The apex locator is essential, but you should always confirm with a radiograph.' Sami, slightly ashamed, admits he forgot the X-ray.

questions.question: Mina prepares the irrigation solution. Sami asks her: 'What is the most commonly used solution?' Mina answers:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Sodium hypochlorite is the reference solution for canal disinfection. But be careful, it must be used with caution.' Sami, impressed, notes the information.

questions.question: Sami, in a hurry, wants to use a high concentration of sodium hypochlorite. Mina stops him: 'Be careful, too high a concentration can:'
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A concentration that's too high can be toxic if extruded beyond the apex.' Sami, cautious, chooses an appropriate concentration.

questions.question: Mina performs canal obturation. Sami asks her: 'Why are you using gutta-percha rather than another material?' Mina answers:
options: It's the reference material, easy to use, and biocompatible
Because it's the only one available
Because I have no other choice
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Gutta-percha is the standard material in endodontics. It's biocompatible, softens with heat, and ensures good sealing.' Sami, convinced, follows her.

questions.question: Sami obturates a canal without using sealer cement. Mina, horrified, tells him: 'You forgot the cement!' Sami asks: 'Why is it so important?'
options: Cement ensures sealing between gutta-percha and the canal wall
Cement is used to fix the crown
Cement is just an optional addition
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Sealer cement fills the spaces between gutta-percha and dentin, ensuring perfect sealing.' Sami, resuming his work, thanks her.

questions.question: A patient returns with pain after a root canal treatment performed by Sami. Mina examines and says: 'You have a periapical lesion.' Sami asks: 'What exactly is that?'
options: Inflammation of the bone around the apex
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A periapical lesion is an inflammatory reaction of the bone around the apex, often due to persistent infection.' Sami, slightly embarrassed, promises to be more rigorous.

questions.question: Sami needs to perform anesthesia for a root canal treatment. Mina asks him: 'What type of anesthesia do you use?' Sami answers:
options: No anesthesia, the pulp is dead
questions.explanation: Mina confirms: 'A nerve block is necessary to block the inferior alveolar nerve. A pulp can be partially vital.' Sami, convinced, anesthetizes correctly.

questions.question: Mina encounters a calcified canal. Sami asks her: 'How are you going to do it?' Mina answers:
options: With active tip files and a lot of patience
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Calcified canals require special files and patience. You need to progress slowly to avoid ledges.' Sami, admiring, observes.

questions.question: Sami, while treating a molar, confuses the canals. Mina tells him: 'Sami, you forgot the mesio-lingual canal!' Sami asks: 'How do you know there is one?'
options: Maxillary molars often have a 4th canal (mesio-lingual)
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Maxillary molars frequently have a 4th canal, the mesio-lingual. It's often fine and easy to overlook.' Sami, grateful, locates the canal.

questions.question: Sami and Mina debate the ideal duration of a root canal treatment. Sami says: 'I do it in 30 minutes!' Mina answers: 'I do it in 1h30, but I do it well.' What matters most?
options: The quality of disinfection and obturation
The price charged to the patient
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Quality comes before speed. A well-done root canal treatment prevents recurrences.' Sami, annoyed, admits she's right.

questions.question: Mina examines a radiograph and says: 'There is a periapical radiolucency.' Sami asks: 'What does that mean?'
options: A radiolucency around the apex, often a granuloma or cyst
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A periapical radiolucency indicates bone loss around the apex, often due to chronic infection.' Sami, slightly worried, examines the X-ray.

questions.question: Sami, while instrumenting a canal, sees blood coming out of the apex. Mina tells him: 'Stop, you've gone past the apex!' Sami asks: 'Why is that serious?'
options: It can cause post-operative pain and infection
It's normal, it happens all the time
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Going past the apex with a file can push bacteria and debris into the periapical tissues.' Sami, cautious, adjusts his working length.

questions.question: Mina chooses the working length. Sami asks her: 'How do you determine it?' Mina answers:
options: With an apex locator and confirmed by radiograph
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The combination of the apex locator and radiograph is the most reliable method.' Sami, attentive, takes notes.

questions.question: Sami, in a hurry, wants to skip the control radiograph step. Mina stops him: 'Sami, you should always check!' Why?
options: To check the working length and obturation quality
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The control radiograph allows verification of the working length before obturation, and the quality of the final obturation.' Sami, slightly embarrassed, takes an X-ray.

questions.question: Mina, at the end of the treatment, explains the post-operative rules to the patient. Sami asks: 'What do you tell them?' Mina answers:
options: Avoid chewing on the tooth until the crown is placed
Use a toothpick to clean the crown
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The treated tooth is fragile and must be protected until the definitive restoration.' Sami, approving, adds some advice.

questions.question: Sami, after finishing, asks Mina: 'When should the crown be placed?' Mina answers:
options: When the tooth is asymptomatic, ideally within weeks of treatment
Never, the tooth stays without a crown
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'You should wait until the tooth is no longer symptomatic, then a crown is necessary to prevent fracture.' Sami, agreeing, notes the recommendation.

questions.question: Sami, a bit too confident, tells a patient: 'Your root canal treatment is guaranteed for life!' Mina intervenes: 'Sami, you need to be careful!' Why?
options: No treatment is guaranteed for life, failures can occur
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Root canal treatments can fail, even with perfect technique. You should always inform the patient of the risks.' Sami, slightly embarrassed, corrects his words.

questions.question: Mina, while cleaning the canals, finds a foul odor. Sami asks her: 'What does that mean?' Mina answers:
options: It's a sign of significant bacterial infection
It's normal, it's the smell of dentin
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A foul odor indicates the presence of anaerobic bacteria, often responsible for canal infections.' Sami, disgusted, continues cleaning.

questions.question: Sami, at the end of the treatment, asks Mina: 'What is the success rate of a well-done root canal treatment?' Mina answers:
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'With good technique, success rates are high, but you should always inform the patient of the risks of failure.' Sami, impressed, is more cautious.

questions.question: Sami, while talking to a patient, confuses pulpectomy and pulpotomy. Mina corrects him. Which of these statements is correct?
options: Pulpectomy is complete pulp removal, pulpotomy is partial
Pulpotomy is more complete than pulpectomy
Pulpectomy is reserved for primary teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Pulpectomy removes all the pulp, pulpotomy removes only the coronal pulp.' Sami, grateful, thanks Mina for the clarification.
